question.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
question.problem: Consider a matrix equation $AB\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $4\times 4$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $4\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $AB\,x=d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB\,x & =d \\ {A}^{-1}AB\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x={A}^{-1}\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
